newsitem.title: USA: US prods take a pounding with NYMEX in late trade.
newsitem.headline: US prods take a pounding with NYMEX in late trade.

text.p: U.S. spot products prices took a pounding with September futures prices by late Monday, players said, with gasoline leading the steep plunge.
Although differentials on most products remained fairly stable in both centers, absolute prices withered under the NYMEX selloff, players said.
Most gasoline grades gave up about 1.50 cents, adding to last week's 1.25-cent pullback from earlier gains.
Distillates meanwhile, lost about one cent, more than offsetting last week's half-cent gain.

"The Merc (NYMEX) got pounded hard," one Gulf Coast trader speculated, because mutual funds were "said to be liquidating long positions prior to Friday's expiration of September No. 2 and reformulated" gasoline contracts.
But activity was quiet and thin amidst the strong price swing, said an East Coast trader, who called it "just another sleepy Monday."
Traders, meanwhile, said they were not yet overly concerned about Hurricane Edouard, which was upgraded to an "extreme" Category 4 storm after its winds increased to 140-mph by 5 p.m. EDT.
